name: TPS73150DBVT
title: Capacitor-free NMOS 150 mA LDO regulator with reverse-current blocking
summary: The TPS731 is a 150 mA linear regulator with an NMOS pass transistor in a voltage-follower stage, running from 1.7 V to 5.5 V and dropping 30 mV typical at full load. It needs no output capacitor for stability, blocks current from output to input when disabled, and draws under 1 µA in shutdown. Fixed versions have a noise-reduction pin (down to 8.5 µVRMS per volt of output with 10 nF); the TPS73101 is adjustable from 1.2 V to 5.5 V. TPS73150DBVT is the 5.0 V version in the 5-pin SOT-23 (DBV) on a 250-piece reel.

circuits.title: Typical application circuit, fixed-voltage versions
circuits.description: A fixed-output TPS731 between a supply and its load. IN takes the supply and OUT feeds the load; EN is the on/off control, high for on. All three capacitors are optional: one on the input can help with source impedance, noise and PSRR, one on the output can help load-step response, noise and PSRR, and one from NR to ground filters the reference to cut output noise.

circuits.title: Typical application circuit, adjustable version (TPS73101)
circuits.description: The adjustable TPS73101 with its output set by a resistor divider: R1 from OUT to FB and R2 from FB to ground give VOUT = (R1 + R2) / R2 × 1.204. CFB, optional, sits across R1 to lower output noise and improve transient response. The input and output capacitors are optional, as on the fixed versions, and EN switches the output on when high.

operation.text: The pass element is an NMOS transistor run as a voltage follower. A 4 MHz charge pump lifts its gate drive above VOUT, which lets the part drop less than 100 mV at 150 mA from inputs as low as 1.7 V and outputs down to 1.2 V. Because the follower stage has a low output impedance without feedback, it stays stable with any output capacitor, or none, so the regulator suits loads whose capacitance is not known. Ground pin current stays almost the same across the load range.

Almost all output noise comes from the bandgap reference, about 32 µVRMS from 10 Hz to 100 kHz at NR, multiplied by the same gain that sets VOUT from the reference. On the fixed versions a capacitor from NR to ground makes an RC filter with the internal 27 kΩ; the TPS73115 with 0.01 µF reaches about 12.75 µVRMS. The TPS73101 has no NR pin; a capacitor CFB from OUT to FB lowers its noise and improves its load-step response instead. The charge pump makes roughly 250 µV of ripple near 4 MHz inside the part, which is negligible at OUT for most load currents and output capacitors.

The current limit protects the part in a fault and folds back once VOUT drops below 0.5 V, so a short draws less than the full limit (Figure 5-17). The limit reaches 0 mA at about -0.2 V on the output; if OUT is held below -0.2 V when EN rises, the regulator may fail to start. In systems with both positive and negative rails the TPS731 is enabled first. Foldback can also prevent start-up under some other load conditions.

EN switches the part on when high and accepts standard TTL and CMOS levels. Below 0.5 V the regulator turns off, the GND current falls to about 10 nA and the pass transistor gate is fully discharged. Above 1.7 V the output rises again to its regulated value. When EN is tied to IN instead, the gate may not discharge and the pass device can stay on for a long while after VIN goes away: current can then flow backward if the input is low impedance, power-up ramps are faster, and the output may overshoot at power-up when VIN rises over more than a few milliseconds.

With its gate pulled low the NMOS pass element blocks current from OUT back to IN. EN is taken low ahead of removing the input so that no charge is left on the gate; after that no pin needs bias for blocking. IREV is the current leaving IN when voltage is applied at OUT; current also flows into OUT through the 80 kΩ internal divider to ground. On the TPS73101, current may run backward once VFB exceeds VIN by over 1.0 V.
The part needs at least 1.7 V on IN to work and regulate. It is never run from a DC input above 5.5 V, and near 5.5 V input spikes are kept below the 6.0 V absolute maximum.

Neither capacitor is needed for stability. A low-ESR capacitor of 0.1 µF to 1 µF across the input close to the regulator offsets reactive sources and improves load-step behaviour, ripple rejection and noise; a larger one may be needed for big, fast load steps or when the source is several inches away. An output capacitor of about 1 µF makes load-step undershoot smaller but longer.

Below dropout the NMOS works in its linear region and the path from IN to OUT is its on-resistance. For large load steps the input needs about twice the DC dropout as headroom to keep normal transient response. Recovery time grows with the size and speed of the load change and shrinks with headroom; a full-scale instant step with VIN - VOUT near DC dropout may need roughly 200 µs before the output is back within its accuracy limits.

The output has no active pull-down when it is above its set voltage, so another source may drive OUT higher. With an output capacitor fitted, a fast drop of load current to zero makes the output overshoot by several percent; the overshoot discharges through the internal divider and any load (decay-rate equations), and an added load resistor shortens it.
The input supply is regulated and lies between 1.7 V and 5.5 V. Extra low-ESR input capacitance improves output noise when the supply is noisy.

For best PSRR, noise and transient response the input and output capacitors return to a ground plane that joins the device at its GND pin, and the NR bypass capacitor's ground goes straight to GND. On the DBV footprint CIN sits between pins 1 and 2, COUT runs from pin 5 to ground and CNR from pin 4 to ground. Board area free of other parts, and heavier copper, carry heat away from the package.

The output turns off when the junction reaches about 160 °C and back on when it has cooled to about 140 °C, so under sustained overload the part cycles. Junction temperature is held to 125 °C for reliable operation; a design has margin when shutdown needs an ambient 35 °C or more beyond the highest expected one, with worst-case load, before it trips. Running the part repeatedly into thermal shutdown shortens its life, and the protection does not replace heat sinking.

An M3 suffix means new silicon only, CSO code RFB. Without M3 a reel may hold either silicon, legacy (CSO code DLN) or new (CSO code RFB), and its label gives the code. The two differ in ground pin current, shutdown current conditions, thermal resistance and their typical curves.
